audit_findings.title: FY2026 OE may understate the run-rate interest burden on the latest debt balance
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.470 million pre-tax annualized gap: 4 × $1.518 million latest-quarter interest less $4.602 million FY2026 interest
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-period interest burden reduces equity-level OE because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2026, we used approximately $83.0 million, drawn from the Credit Facility, for a business acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated run-rate mismatch, not merely a hypothetical risk. Annualizing the latest quarter produces $6.072 million of interest versus $4.602 million included in FY2026. At the filed 30%-32% FY2027 tax-rate range, the approximate after-tax difference is $1.00-$1.03 million, or about 5% of the $20.2 million anchor. That is large enough to materially move the scenario values, although the downward correction would not close the gap between the $34.56 bull value and the $85.48 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized OE using the June-quarter average debt, 5.2% weighted-average rate, facility fees and the filed tax-rate range, then rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with the post-year-end SCM acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.808 million acquisition cash outflow and $13.0 million acquisition borrowing; SCM valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The March OE anchor excludes SCM operations, while the June bridge includes post-acquisition cash and debt; missing SCM earnings understates OE, while missing associated interest or other recurring costs overstates it.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 9, 2026, the Company acquired SCM Metrology and Laboratories S.A, a privately-held calibration services provider, based in Costa Rica to advance the Company's strategy to grow alongside customers in high-growth, highly regulated markets.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. The latest 10-Q confirms that SCM closed for approximately $12.8 million and was primarily financed with a $13.0 million facility draw. It also reports $6.930 million of combined acquired Service revenue from Essco and SCM, but does not isolate SCM earnings or cash generation. The record therefore cannot determine the net value effect or establish whether it is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain SCM-only post-close revenue, operating profit, maintenance capex and working-capital data; construct a full-year after-tax OE contribution including acquisition interest, or rerun every input on the March 28 pre-SCM perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Revenue-control material weaknesses reduce confidence in the OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Revenue amount and cutoff flow through earnings, receivables and working-capital changes used to calculate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We did not design and maintain adequate controls within the revenue process that resulted in material weaknesses, either individually or in the aggregate, over (a) management’s review of established pricing and contract terms to support recorded revenue, (b) review of the completeness and accuracy of customer order entry, quantity and pricing, and (c) the determination of the appropriate period for revenue recognition.
audit_findings.explanation: No revenue misstatement or restatement is demonstrated, and the annual auditor issued an unqualified financial-statement opinion. However, both the 10-K and latest 10-Q state that the material weaknesses remained unresolved, creating a continuing possibility that the single-year anchor is misstated. The filings do not quantify an error, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Review post-quarter collections, credit notes, revenue reversals, cutoff testing and audit adjustments, including separate testing of Essco and SCM revenue, before relying on the FY2026 anchor.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven growth may require investment not captured by ordinary capex
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.934 million FY2026 acquired Service revenue versus 3.0% FY2026 Service organic growth; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth assumptions are applied to OE; acquisition-funded growth requires purchase-price reinvestment beyond ordinary property-and-equipment capex.
audit_findings.evidence: This year-over-year increase included $30.9 million of incremental revenue from the acquisitions of Essco and Martin.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking conditional risk rather than a demonstrated omission in current OE. FY2026 organic Service growth was 3.0%, matching the base growth assumption, while the latest quarter reported 12.8% organic growth and management forecast high-single-digit organic growth. The 6% bull case therefore need not require acquisitions, but continued monitoring is necessary because acquisitions remain an explicit part of strategy.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic and acquired growth in forecasts and require evidence that each scenario's growth can be achieved organically; if acquisitions are assumed, rerun with acquisition purchase payments and financing costs included as reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid acquisition holdbacks may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.5 million unpaid holdbacks at June 27, 2026, equal to about $0.46 per diluted share and 1.5% of the $291 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid acquisition purchase-price obligation should reduce the equity bridge unless its settlement is already captured in OE or the reported cash balance.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 28, 2026 , no contingent consideration and $ 2.2 million of other holdback amounts were unpaid and are reflected in accrued compensation and other current liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q resolves the existence question and reports $4.5 million of unpaid holdbacks, so the omission is demonstrated if the bridge contains no corresponding deduction. A full $4.5 million deduction would reduce value by approximately $0.46 per share, leaving the base value near $28.93 and the bull value near $34.10, still far below the $85.48 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $4.5 million aggregate disclosure to the $2.247 million accrued-holdback balance-sheet line and $2.8 million Essco disclosure, then deduct the confirmed non-operating amount from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring executive-transition charge may have been capitalized into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.706 million pre-tax in FY2026 plus $0.736 million in Q1 FY2027
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in normalized OE, a finite transition charge depresses the anchor and every projected year and terminal value derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: The year-over-year increase in general and administrative expenses was due to incremental expenses from acquired businesses (including stock expense of $3.8 million), increased payroll costs of $5.9 million, executive transition costs of $1.7 million and continued investments in technology of $1.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed charge is substantial relative to the $20.2 million anchor, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation already normalized it. The additional $0.736 million recorded in the next quarter also shows that the transition program spans periods, so the entire amount cannot be removed solely because management labels it a transition cost. The possible valuation effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace both transition-charge amounts through the OE calculation, identify contractual or completed costs that will not recur, normalize only their after-tax amount, and rerun the scenarios if the FY2026 anchor currently includes them.
